doc.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

title: Joining Benny Goodman's band
summary: John Bunch's call, the Astor Hotel jam, no charts, and Goodman's generous introduction.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: The other thing is, those stories which are in my heart. The first time — I get a call from John Bunch, he says Benny Goodman needs a trumpet player can you come down to the Astor Hotel right away? I says sure. So I pack up my horn and I go down to the Astor Hotel, I walk in and there’s Benny, Buddy Tate, John Bunch, Connie Kaye, and who’s the bass player?
No, the guy who sings and plays.

Major Holley. Okay. So then he doesn’t say anything to me. We jam for 45 minutes. He comes up to me and he says, “I love your playing, can you leave tomorrow for the road?” Now I knew he had a trumpet player. I think it was Jack Sheldon. And I wanted to be polite, I didn’t want to take someone’s gig, so I said to Benny, “I thought you had a trumpet player.” He said, “I didn’t ask you that, can you leave tomorrow for the road?” So I leave, so I get to the gig and we’re ready to go on. And I say to Connie, “Are there any charts?” Connie says, “Oh charts, yeah.” He reaches into his trap case and pulls out this brown ripped piece of paper that had the last 16 bars to “Undecided” riff on it. And he hands it to me. “Here’s your charts.” So I get the message, there’s no charts. So I go on and it’s time for my feature which is “Talk of the Town.” Now Benny was not known, I had a great relationship, but not known to be a very giving guy if you’ve heard Benny Goodman stories. Different from Count Basie. He gets on the mic he says, “Before this gentleman does his feature I want to tell you a little bit about him, this young man that I found.” He says, “I’ve had everybody in my bands,” and he starts listing all these trumpet players: Harry James, Cootie Williams, on and on. “I just want you to know before you hear him, he can hold his own with any one of those guys.” I almost couldn’t play after that intro.
Wow. That is not the typical Benny story.
